title: From Voxels to Knowledge: A Practical Guide to the Segmentation of Complex Electron Microscopy 3D-Data
protocol: Place markers along the feature of interest.
Connect markers with linkers where appropriate.
Open the Volume Tracer dialog from Tools > Volume Tracer dialog.
Select File > New Marker Set in the Volume Tracer dialog.
Check Mouse > Place markers on high quality, Place markers on data planes, Move and resize markers, Link new marker to selected marker, and Link consecutively selected markers.
Click on the Marker Color swatch and select a color.
Repeat for Link color.
Enter radii for the marker and link model-building elements.
Select Place markers using [right] mouse button in the Volume Tracer Window.
Insert radii for markers and links.
Right click on the volume data to begin laying down markers.
Save current marker set by selecting File > Save current marker set.
Close marker set by selecting File > Close marker set.
Open a new marker set to begin building a model into a second desired feature of interest.
Import volume data into a program with manual tracing options.
Select Open Data > Right click on filename.rec > Format… > Select Raw as LargeDiskData > Ok > Load for large volumes or tomograms.
Select appropriate Raw Data Parameters from header information > Ok.
Toggle and Save As a new filename.am file for use in the following steps for large volumes or tomograms.
Open Data > Select filename.tif or filename.mrc for smaller 3D image stack files.
Toggle and Right Click > Save As filename.am file for use in the following steps for smaller 3D image stack files.
Navigate through the slices to select a 3D sub-volume for segmentation, and then crop to this area of interest.
In 3D Viewer window, select Orthoslice to open image file.
Use slider at bottom to navigate through slices.
Toggle file name in Pool window for LargeDiskData > Right click > LatticeAccess.
Enter desired box size > Apply.
Save new file.
Create segmentation file.
Toggle the file in the Pool window > Right Click > Labeling > LabelField.
Trace the border of the first feature of interest by hand or using a command specific to the software used.
Follow the feature of interest through all slices and repeat manual tracing segmentation.
Use Paintbrush tool, alter brush size as desired, then use mouse pointer to trace border of feature of interest in Amira.
Fill traced area with shortcut “f” in Amira.
Add selection by clicking button with plus symbol or using shortcut “a” in Amira.
Undo action if necessary by pressing “u” in Amira.
Subtract or erase by pressing “s” in Amira.
Generate a surface rendering for visualization and basic qualitative or quantitative analysis per software user guide instruction.
Toggle filename-labels.am in Pool window > Right click > SurfaceGen.
Select desired Surface properties > Apply.
A new file filename.surf will be created in the Pool.
Visualize segmented volume by toggling filename.surf in Pool window > Right click > SurfaceView.
Use tools in 3DViewer window to move, rotate, and zoom into 3D volume.
Extract exact densities from the data set.
Determine measurements such as volume or surface area.
Export measurements to other programs for advanced display and analysis.
On 3DViewer window, click Measure tool.
Select appropriate option (2D length and 2D angle for single plane measurements, 3D length and 3D Angle for volumetric measurements).
Click on mesh surface to measure desired lengths, distances, and angles.
The values will be listed in the Properties window.
Import volume data into a program equipped with thresholding or magic wand tools.
Follow steps outlined for manual tracing as described in sections 2.1-2.1.2.
Navigate through slices and select area for segmentation.
Crop out a smaller 3D sub-volume if necessary.
Follow additional steps outlined in sections 2.2-2.2.2 for manual tracing.
Select the density of a feature of interest by clicking on it.
Adjust sliders in Display and Masking to capture the correct range of values for the feature.
Add selection with shortcut “a”.
Use the Threshold Tool for features without clearly distinguishable margins.
Adjust slider to adjust density within desirable range so that only the features of interest are masked.
Click Select button, then add selection with shortcut “a”.
Select All slices before adding selection for entire volume segmentation.
Remove noise by selecting Segmentation > Remove Islands and/or Segmentation > Smooth labels.
Generate a surface for visualization and qualitative analysis as described in the manual tracing section 2.6-2.6.2.
Export to other programs for adequate 3D display, quantitative analysis and simulations if desired.
Load the image using the imread command.
Call Wiener Filter using an estimated or known Noise-power-to-signal ratio (NSR).
Estimate the background layer on the previously processed image using imopen function.
Allocate the outcome as a different mask.
Subtract the filtered image with the background.
Perform image normalization with adaptive Otsu’s method if necessary.
Prepare the features of interest for segmentation by cropping the normalized image.
Use imtool command to explore the region of interest and provide coordinates: >> im3_crop = imcrop(im3, [x1 y1 x2 y2]).
Train the algorithm by providing specific examples for each different category of objects using VL_HIKMEANS function: >> [TREE,ASGN] = VL_HIKMEANS(im3_crop,$K,$NLEAVES).
Check that VLFEAT API is successfully installed and visit VLFeat’s website for documentation.
Use manually segmented features as the input for VLFeat.
Load the previously generated numeral array (model).
Call the support vector machine (SVM) function in VLFeat using the model and the image to be segmented as input.
Enter the command [w, b] = vl_svmtrain(x, y, 0.1), where x is the original cropped image im2_crop and y is the objective image.
Use ISEG = VL_IMSEG(I,LABELS) to color the results according to the labels generated by the clustering.
Save results using the command imwrite(im, 'tiff', filename).
Enter the command imshow(im) for visualizing images.
